reading.title: 注意力经济：我们为何难以专注
reading.sub: 仔细阅读 Section C 实战 · 博浩原创真题风格篇章

data.passage:
The modern economy has been described as an economy of attention: companies compete not for money alone, but for the limited time and mental energy of consumers. Nowhere is this competition fiercer than in the design of smartphones, where every notification is engineered to interrupt, and every interface is tested to keep users scrolling.

Psychologists warn that this endless competition has a measurable cost. Studies show that people who constantly switch between tasks remember less, make more errors, and feel more stressed than those who focus on one thing at a time. What troubles researchers most is that many users no longer decide for themselves when to pay attention; the device decides for them. A notification arrives, attention shifts, and the original goal — writing an essay, reading a book, having a conversation — quietly disappears.

Yet experts insist that the solution is not to abandon technology altogether. Rather, they recommend what one researcher calls digital minimalism: a deliberate reduction in the number of apps and alerts we allow into our lives. Small changes, such as turning off non-essential notifications or keeping the phone out of the bedroom, can restore a sense of control. The goal is not to use technology less, but to use it with intention.

qs.q: What does the author mean by calling the modern economy an economy of attention?
opts: Companies mainly compete for consumers' limited time and mental focus.
Attention is the only product that technology companies sell.
Consumers are paying more money to protect their attention.
Modern workers are more focused than those in the past.
qs.ex: 首段指出公司不仅为金钱竞争，也为消费者有限的时间与注意力竞争，故选 A。

qs.q: What troubles researchers most according to Paragraph 2?
opts: People remember less when they listen to music.
Users have lost control over where they direct their attention.
Notifications are too difficult to design.
Employees make more errors at work than students.
qs.ex: 第二段明确：最让研究者担忧的是用户不再自主决定何时专注，而是由设备决定。

qs.q: What is the author's suggestion about using technology?
opts: People should stop using smartphones completely.
Governments should ban unnecessary notifications.
People should use technology deliberately and cut unnecessary alerts.
Reading books is the only way to restore attention.
qs.ex: 末段提出 digital minimalism 与 use it with intention，即有意减少应用与提醒。A 为绝对化干扰项。

reading.title: 城市绿化：看不见的公共财富
reading.sub: 仔细阅读 Section C 实战 · 博浩原创真题风格篇章

data.passage:
City parks are usually regarded as pleasant but optional extras — nice to have when budgets allow. A growing body of research, however, suggests that urban green spaces deliver benefits far beyond recreation. Trees cool the air, absorb storm water, and filter pollutants, while parks encourage exercise and social contact.

Perhaps the most striking evidence comes from studies of health. Researchers followed residents of a large city for five years and found that those living within easy walking distance of a park were significantly less likely to develop heart disease, even after controlling for income and lifestyle. The effect was strongest among older adults, for whom a nearby bench under a shade tree may be the difference between daily walks and staying indoors.

Given such findings, some economists argue that green space should be treated as infrastructure rather than decoration. They point out that a single mature tree can provide tens of thousands of dollars worth of benefits over its lifetime — in cooling, flood prevention, and improved air quality. The challenge, they admit, is that these returns are slow and invisible, making them easy for budget planners to overlook.

qs.q: What is the popular view of city parks mentioned at the beginning?
opts: They are essential public infrastructure.
They are pleasant but not essential.
They cost too much to maintain.
They mainly benefit older adults.
qs.ex: 首句说公园常被视为 pleasant but optional extras，即宜人但可有可无。

qs.q: What did the five-year study find?
opts: People near parks do more outdoor sports.
Older adults rarely visit city parks.
Living near a park reduces the risk of heart disease.
Park visitors have higher incomes.
qs.ex: 研究显示，步行可达公园的居民患心脏病风险显著更低，且在控制收入与生活方式后依然成立。

qs.q: Why do budget planners tend to overlook green space according to economists?
opts: Because parks occupy too much land.
Because the benefits are slow and hard to see.
Because trees damage city pipes.
Because maintenance costs keep rising.
qs.ex: 经济学家指出绿色空间的回报 slow and invisible，因此容易被预算规划者忽视。

reading.title: 终身学习：技能更新的新常态
reading.sub: 仔细阅读 Section C 实战 · 博浩原创真题风格篇章

data.passage:
For most of the twentieth century, education followed a simple pattern: people learned in their youth and worked for the rest of their lives. That pattern is breaking down. With technology changing the nature of jobs at an accelerating pace, the skills that guarantee employment today may be obsolete within a decade.

This reality has given rise to what educators call lifelong learning. Unlike traditional schooling, which is organized around fixed curricula and credentials, lifelong learning is continuous, self-directed, and often informal. A software engineer may take online courses in data science; a nurse may attend workshops on new medical devices; a manager may study behavioral economics in the evenings. In each case, the learner, not the institution, defines the goal.

Employers are beginning to respond. Many now offer internal training budgets and encourage workers to spend part of their week on professional development. Yet experts caution that individuals cannot rely on companies alone. The most successful learners, they say, share two habits: they treat learning as a daily practice rather than a crisis response, and they are willing to learn publicly — asking questions, sharing progress, and admitting what they do not yet know.

qs.q: What is the main reason that the traditional education pattern is breaking down?
opts: People no longer value university degrees.
Technology changes the skills required for jobs very quickly.
Schools have become too expensive.
Employers prefer informal learning.
qs.ex: 第二句说明：技术加速改变工作性质，今天的技能可能十年内过时。

qs.q: What distinguishes lifelong learning from traditional schooling?
opts: It is continuous, self-directed and often informal.
It is organized around fixed curricula.
It leads to formal credentials.
It only happens in universities.
qs.ex: 文中对比：终身学习 continuous, self-directed, informal，由学习者而非机构定义目标。

qs.q: What two habits do the most successful learners share?
opts: They learn daily and are willing to learn publicly.
They change careers frequently.
They study only through formal courses.
They rely mainly on employer training.
qs.ex: 末段：成功学习者把学习当日常而非应急，并愿意公开学习（提问、分享、承认不足）。

reading.title: 睡眠与记忆：大脑的夜间整理
reading.sub: 仔细阅读 Section C 实战 · 博浩原创真题风格篇章

data.passage:
For a long time, scientists believed that memory was formed mainly while we were awake. Recent research, however, shows that sleep plays an equally important role. During deep sleep, the brain reviews the information learned during the day and transfers it from short-term to long-term storage — a process researchers compare to a librarian filing books on shelves.

In one experiment, students who napped for forty minutes after studying remembered twenty percent more than those who stayed awake. The effect was especially clear for factual material, such as lists of words or historical dates. Interestingly, the quality of sleep matters more than its length: interrupted sleep, even when it totals eight hours, sharply reduces the ability to recall.

These findings have practical implications for students. Pulling an all-nighter before an exam, the researchers note, is almost always counterproductive, because the brain needs sleep to consolidate what has been learned. They advise a different strategy: study in the evening, sleep normally, and review briefly in the morning. In other words, sleep is not the enemy of study — it is part of study.

qs.q: What did scientists used to believe about memory?
opts: Memory is formed mainly during deep sleep.
Memory is formed while people are awake.
Sleep has little to do with memory formation.
Napping improves long-term memory.
qs.ex: 首句：过去科学家认为记忆主要在清醒时形成。

qs.q: What did the experiment with students show?
opts: Sleeping longer always improves memory.
Staying awake helped students remember more.
A forty-minute nap helped students remember more.
Naps only help with numbers.
qs.ex: 实验：小睡 40 分钟的学生比清醒者多记住 20%，对事实类材料尤其明显。

qs.q: What strategy do the researchers advise for exams?
opts: Stay up all night to review everything.
Study in the evening, sleep normally, and review in the morning.
Take a nap immediately before the exam.
Avoid reviewing on the exam day.
qs.ex: 末段建议：晚上学习、正常睡眠、早晨简要复习；熬夜几乎总是适得其反。

listening.title: 讲座：为什么我们会忘记
listening.sub: 讲座 / 讲话 Lecture · 博浩原创语料

data.text:
Today we turn to a question that troubles every student: why do we forget? Psychologists used to describe forgetting as a failure of memory, but most now agree that it is actually a design feature of the brain. If we remembered everything, they argue, we would be overwhelmed by useless information. Forgetting helps the brain keep what matters and discard the rest.

So why do important things still slip away? The main reason is that memory is strengthened by use. Information that is retrieved again and again forms stronger connections, while information that is never revisited gradually fades — a process known as decay. This is why cramming the night before an exam is so ineffective: the material is stored only in short-term memory and never practiced again.

The solution is simple but requires effort: space out your study. Reviewing material after one day, then three days, then a week, sends a signal to the brain that this information is worth keeping. Researchers call this the spacing effect, and it is one of the most reliable findings in all of psychology.

qs.q: How do most psychologists now view forgetting?
opts: It is a failure of memory.
It is a useful feature of the brain.
It can be completely avoided.
It only affects old people.
qs.ex: 多数心理学家认为遗忘是大脑的设计特性，可避免信息过载。

qs.q: Why is cramming before an exam ineffective?
opts: Because exams are too difficult.
Because material is stored only briefly and never practiced again.
Because students do not sleep enough.
Because review is unnecessary.
qs.ex: 临时抱佛脚的内容只存在于短期记忆，未再提取便逐渐衰减。

qs.q: What is the spacing effect?
opts: Studying harder before exams.
Reviewing material at increasing intervals.
Memorizing everything at once.
Studying with music.
qs.ex: 间隔复习（1 天、3 天、1 周…）会告诉大脑这些信息值得保留，即 spacing effect。

longSentence.title: 同位语从句 + 后置定语

data.en: The theory that human memory is not a single system but a collection of systems, each with its own rules, has been supported by decades of experiments.
data.zh: 人类记忆并非单一系统、而是一系列各自拥有规则的系统的集合——这一理论已得到数十年实验的支持。
points: 主干：The theory has been supported by decades of experiments。
that 引导同位语从句解释 theory 的内容。
each with its own rules 为独立主格作补充说明。

longSentence.title: 定语从句中套状语从句

data.en: Employees who feel their opinions are ignored are far more likely to leave the company when the job market improves.
data.zh: 当就业市场好转时，那些感到自己意见被忽视的员工离开公司的可能性要大得多。
points: 主干：Employees are far more likely to leave the company。
who 引导定语从句修饰 employees。
句末 when 引导时间状语从句，说明条件。

data.en: The proposal, though welcomed by many educators, has drawn sharp criticism from parents who worry about screen time.
data.zh: 尽管这一提案受到许多教育工作者欢迎，却招致了担心屏幕时间的家长们的尖锐批评。
points: 主干：The proposal has drawn sharp criticism from parents。
though welcomed by many educators 为插入的让步状语。
who 从句修饰 parents。

data.en: Faced with shrinking budgets, universities are cutting liberal-arts programs that once defined a well-rounded education.
data.zh: 面对不断缩减的预算，高校正在削减那些曾定义通识教育的文科项目。
points: 主干：universities are cutting liberal-arts programs。
Faced with… 为过去分词短语作原因状语，逻辑主语是 universities。
that 从句修饰 programs。

data.en: Not until the invention of the printing press did knowledge become widely available to ordinary people.
data.zh: 直到印刷术发明，知识才广泛地为普通民众所获得。
points: Not until… 置于句首引起部分倒装：did knowledge become。
主句正常语序应为 knowledge did not become… until…。
翻译时还原为直到…才…。

data.en: It is the quality of sleep, rather than its quantity, that determines how well we remember what we have learned.
data.zh: 决定我们对所学内容记忆好坏的是睡眠质量，而非睡眠时长。
points: It is … that … 为强调句型，被强调部分是 the quality of sleep。
rather than its quantity 为插入的对比成分。
how well we remember… 为宾语从句。

longSentence.title: 虚拟语气 + 目的状语

data.en: Had the company invested in renewable energy ten years ago, it would not have struggled so much to meet today's emission standards.
data.zh: 如果这家公司十年前就投资可再生能源，如今就不至于为达到排放标准而如此挣扎。
points: Had… done 为虚拟条件句倒装，等于 If the company had invested…。
主句 would not have struggled 表示与过去事实相反。
不定式 to meet… 表目的。

longSentence.title: 多重并列 + 定语从句

data.en: Cities that invest in public transport, that design streets for pedestrians rather than cars, and that protect their green spaces tend to be healthier and more prosperous.
data.zh: 那些投资公共交通、把街道设计给行人而非汽车、并保护绿地的城市，往往更健康、更繁荣。
points: 主干：Cities tend to be healthier and more prosperous。
三个 that 引导的并列定语从句共同修饰 cities。

writingTemplate.title: 议论文（观点 / 现象类）· 最高频

structure: 引入现象 / 亮明观点（1 段）
正面论证，例证支撑（1–2 段）
让步与反驳，体现思辨（1 段）
总结建议，重申观点（1 段）
data.skeleton:
Paragraph 1: 【现象/话题】has become a hot topic in recent years. From my perspective, 【观点】.
Paragraph 2: To begin with, 【论点一】. For example, 【例证】. Besides, 【进一步说明】.
Paragraph 3: Admittedly, 【对方合理之处】. However, 【反驳/强调自己观点】.
Paragraph 4: In conclusion, 【重申观点】. It is high time that we 【建议】.
tips: 开头亮观点要快：前两句内让阅卷老师看到立场。
每段首句 = 主题句，先结论后例证。
让步段 Admittedly… However… 是加分项。
结尾两句收束：重申观点 + 行动建议，不引入新论点。

structure: 描述图表总体趋势（1 段）
解读趋势并分析原因（2–3 段）
data.skeleton:
Paragraph 1: As is clearly shown in the chart, 【总体趋势】. The figure for 【A】 rose sharply from 【数字】 to 【数字】, while 【B】 remained relatively stable.
Paragraph 2: Several factors may account for this phenomenon. To begin with, 【原因一】. Moreover, 【原因二】. Last but not least, 【原因三】.

原因至少两条，落到经济、科技、观念、政策等维度。

essay.title: 在线课程会取代课堂教学吗？

data.topic: Some people think online courses will eventually replace traditional classroom teaching. Do you agree or disagree?
paras: In recent years, online courses have developed at an astonishing speed. Some people even claim that they will eventually replace traditional classroom teaching. Impressive as online learning is, I believe it will serve as a complement rather than a substitute.

To begin with, online courses offer flexibility and abundant resources. Learners can arrange their own schedules and choose lectures given by top professors worldwide. A case in point is the MOOCs that have enabled millions of students to study at home during the pandemic.

Admittedly, face-to-face teaching has its own irreplaceable value. In a classroom, teachers can observe students' reactions in time, while group discussions and lab work cultivate communication and teamwork. More importantly, the emotional bond between teachers and students can hardly be delivered through a screen.
In conclusion, online education is a powerful tool, but it cannot replace the human touch of traditional classrooms. It is high time that we combined the two to create a better learning experience.
comments: 结构 4 段清晰：现象引入 → 让步（承认网课优点）→ 转折立论 → 结尾升华（融合）。
让步倒装 Impressive as online learning is 比平淡的 Although 更有文采。
例证具体：提到 MOOCs 与疫情居家学习。
观点词精准：complement 与 substitute 一词见高下。

essay.title: 大学生是否应该做兼职？

data.topic: More and more college students take part-time jobs. Do the benefits outweigh the drawbacks?
paras: As the cost of living on campus continues to rise, an increasing number of college students choose to take part-time jobs. While some worry that work may distract them from study, I believe the benefits clearly outweigh the drawbacks when the work is kept in balance.

To begin with, part-time jobs offer financial independence. Many students use their earnings to cover living expenses or save for further study, which relieves the burden on their families. Besides, work experience sharpens practical skills that classrooms rarely teach, such as time management, communication, and teamwork.

Admittedly, an ill-planned job can eat into study time and cause fatigue. A student who works late every night is bound to suffer in class the next day. However, this risk can be managed: most successful student-workers limit themselves to ten to fifteen hours a week and choose jobs related to their majors or interests.
In conclusion, part-time work, when properly managed, enriches rather than endangers college life. It is high time that universities offered more guidance to help students balance work and study.
comments: 立场句直接回应题目利弊比较。
让步段用 A student who… 的具体化写法避免空泛。
用数字 ten to fifteen hours 增加论证可信度。
结尾从个人上升到高校引导，格局更高。

body: 前 10 天：回归基础，把高频词与错题本过一遍，专项补齐最弱题型。
中 10 天：隔天一次整套限时模考，训练时间分配与心态。
后 10 天：只做减法——复习模板句型、翻译主题词块与错题，不再刷新题。
考前 1 天：准备好证件与耳机，按考试时间作息，别再熬夜。
写作 30 分钟：5 分钟列提纲，20 分钟成文，5 分钟检查。
听力约 30 分钟：边听边涂卡，录音结束立即利用空隙预读下一题选项。
阅读 40 分钟：选词填空 ≤ 8 分钟，长篇阅读 ≤ 12 分钟，仔细阅读 ≤ 18 分钟，留 2 分钟机动。
翻译 30 分钟：先通读全文定基调，再逐句翻译，最后检查时态与单复数。
不要停在没听懂的那句上，果断跟上下文，很多题靠整体理解也能做对。
预读选项圈关键词，带着问题听，效率远高于盲听。
数字、转折、因果处放慢注意，答案多藏在这里。
平时精听坚持逐句 + 跟读，比泛听十篇更有效。
审题时圈出题目里的关键词与限定词（如 agree or disagree、advantages and disadvantages）。
列 3–5 点提纲再动笔，确保每一段都服务中心论点。
段落首句反复点题关键词，让阅卷老师一眼看出你没跑题。
宁用简单句写对，也不用高级句写错。
先读题干后读文章，用关键词定位，不要逐词精读全文。
注意段首段尾句与转折词后的内容，那是主旨与观点的高发区。
遇到生词别慌：通过词根词缀、上下文对比和常识推断。
限时训练时给自己留 2 分钟检查涂卡，防止串行。
